rules.title: Good cause required to decline lease renewal (NJ Anti-Eviction Act, as summarized in DCA Truth in Renting guide)
rules.requirement: A landlord of residential rental property may not fail to renew a written or oral lease unless the landlord has good cause not to renew. The good causes are listed in the guide's Eviction section, which is not in this chunk. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units are excepted.
rules.citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18:61.3 (as cited in the DCA Truth in Renting guide)
rules.quoted_span: regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units. Tenants of owner-occupied two- or three-family buildings are referred to a separate guide section that is not in this chunk.
rules.interaction: The guide says the good causes are detailed in its Eviction section. That section is outside this chunk, so the list of permitted causes is not captured here. Local just-cause ordinances are not addressed in this chunk.
